tag: an engine never asks the router, so the architecture routes and the cognition does not compute
why: L1 and L2 — the state measured before this round, for one engine. A grep across all six returned ZERO references to a gateway, an orchestrator or a generate call; the only occurrence of the word was the basis string saying so. The mutation keeps every other line intact, so only driving the engine sees it.

tag: an engine reports the never-asked marker after a routed floor serve
why: L2. 'native-fixed-marker' means nothing was ever asked; 'native-floor' means the router walked down and the floor served. Collapsing them loses the entire gain of this round - the engine would look exactly as it did before it was wired.

tag: the basis stops distinguishing a routed floor serve from having no path at all
old:
"different from having no path, which is what was measured here before: a grep for a "
            "gateway, an orchestrator or a generate call across all six engines returned zero")
why: L2. Without that sentence a reader meets 'no model was asked' and cannot tell whether the platform chose not to ask or was never able to - which is the difference this whole round delivers, and the only difference, since the answers themselves do not change on this machine.

tag: an engine discards the model's text and returns its own marker anyway
why: L3. The engine would ask a model, record that one served it, and then ignore what it said - a provenance claim attached to text the named server never produced, which is worse than not asking. Unreachable from live state here, so L3 supplies the model.

tag: an engine does not record what served it
why: L3, and FU-275's own words: 'the engine must carry what served it, because a reasoning step with no provenance cannot be told from the floor composing headings'.

tag: a failed model call is recorded as a floor serve
old:
prov["served_by"] = None
        prov["model_asked"] = True
        prov["basis"] = (
            f"the router chose {decision.get('tier')} and THE CALL FAILED "
new:
prov["served_by"] = "native-floor"
        prov["model_asked"] = True
        prov["basis"] = (
            f"the router chose {decision.get('tier')} and THE CALL FAILED "
why: L3. A call that raised produced NOTHING; attributing it to the floor would say something composed the answer when nothing did, and the absence would read as a composition. The honest sentence stays in place under the mutation, so only the field a reader branches on changes - the shape a leg reading prose would pass over.

tag: an engine invents a confidence once it has a model path
why: L2 and L3. 0.88 is the exact figure all eight constructors invented before P3.12 removed the requirement. Having a path to a model is not a reason to start producing a number nothing computes, and the temptation arrives precisely when the call starts working.

tag: the model path raises into the engine when the router is broken
why: L4 — the defect this module ACTUALLY HAD until the guard drove it: the import was wrapped and the call was not, while the docstring claimed it never raises into an engine. A reasoning step must not fail because the fabric could not be consulted.

tag: an engine has no declared domain, so the router defaults it silently
why: L5. A missing declaration does not fail - it falls through to the default want, so the engine is routed as something it never said it was. The guard compares the declared set against the engines that exist.

tag: the scope appraisal picks an item for a change no open row relates to
why: The arm W560 added after the pinned fixture went stale. With the branch gone, max() over an empty dict raises and the submission 500s; with it mis-wired to pick an item anyway, an appraisal would ride the record a reviewer reads attached to an item that has nothing to do with the change. A change whose area no open row names must report NO scope, with the reason.
